gloss: to pass on (information) to a successor or next shift

definitions.gloss: to pass on; to hand over (information, duties)
definitions.explanation: To pass on information, instructions, or pending matters to the person who takes over next, such as the next shift, a successor in a post, or the next committee. Common in hospitals, care work, and offices.

examples.japanese: ⟦{次|つぎ}→次：00819_tsugi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{担当者|たんとうしゃ}→担当者：09676_tantousha⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{申|もう}し⟦{送|おく}った→送る：00742_okuru⟧。
examples.english: I passed it on to the next person in charge.

examples.japanese: ⟦{患者|かんじゃ}→患者：00170_kanja⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{様子|ようす}→様子：01521_yousu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{夜勤|やきん}→夜勤：09549_yakin⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{申|もう}し{送|おく}る。
examples.english: We report the patients' condition to the night shift.

examples.japanese: ⟦{解決|かいけつ}→解決：00136_kaiketsu⟧できなかった⟦{問題|もんだい}→問題：00797_mondai⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦{来年度|らいねんど}→来年度：28221_rainendo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{委員会|いいんかい}→委員会：12234_iinkai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{申|もう}し{送|おく}ることにした。
examples.english: We decided to hand the unresolved issues over to next year's committee.

notes:
{申|もう}し{送|おく}る is transitive: the information or matter takes ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧ and the recipient takes ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧. It belongs to workplace language; the noun ⟦{申|もう}し{送|おく}り→申し送り：08385_moushiokuri⟧ (handover) is even more common, especially in nursing, where the shift-change briefing is called the ⟦{申|もう}し{送|おく}り→申し送り：08385_moushiokuri⟧.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{後任|こうにん}→後任：12580_kounin⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{申|もう}し{送|おく}る: to pass on to one's successor
- ⟦{次|つぎ}→次：00819_tsugi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{勤務|きんむ}→勤務：04545_kinmu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{申|もう}し{送|おく}る: to hand over to the next shift
- ⟦{申|もう}し{送|おく}り→申し送り：08385_moushiokuri⟧⟦{事項|じこう}→事項：11469_jikou⟧: items to be handed over
- ⟦{申|もう}し{送|おく}り→申し送り：08385_moushiokuri⟧をする: to give a handover

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{引|ひ}き{継|つ}ぐ→引き継ぐ：12458_hikitsugu⟧: to take over; to hand over — the general word for transferring duties; {申|もう}し{送|おく}る focuses on conveying the information that goes with them.
- {伝|つた}える: to tell, convey — general, with no sense of succession.
